Declares no\n///         storage of its own.\n///\n///         Fail-open: a misbehaving controller, an invalid quote, or a failed\n///         fee transfer each resolve to \"charge nothing, pay full gross\". A\n///         direct (non-delegatecall) call runs against this contract's own\n///         empty storage and it holds no funds, so it is an inert no-op.\ncontract BorrowerExitPerimeterOps is VaultController, IPerimeterEvents {\n    /// @dev The literal is the surface id: its keccak hash is the key the\n    ///      controller resolves a rate policy under. Changing the string\n    ///      changes the id, so a policy must be configured against the new\n    ///      hash before this surface can charge.\n    /// keccak256(\"PERIMETER_SURFACE_LENDING_BORROWER_WITHDRAW\")\n    bytes32 internal constant PERIMETER_SURFACE_LENDING_BORROWER_WITHDRAW =\n limit). `token == address(0)` is\n    ///         the native (measured-receipt) leg; otherwise the ERC20\n    ///         (measured-delta) leg. `effOrig`/`effOwner` are the originator and\n    ///         owner the up-front quote returned, unchanged; `subProduct` is the\n    ///         iToken pool.\n    struct DelayLeg {\n        address queue;\n        address token;\n        uint256 toUser;\n quote,\n    ///         validate, pay the fee leg, emit the audit event, and return the\n    ///         amount the caller pays the user (the caller does the user-leg\n    ///         payout on its own vault primitives).\n    /// @param  surfaceId   Perimeter surface key (borrower-withdraw).\n    /// @param  subProduct  Policy resolution key \u2014 the iToken proxy the loan\n    ///                     was originated against (`loanLocal.lender`).\n    /// @param  receiver    User payout recipient (logged in ExitFeeApplied).\n    /// @param  payoutAsset Asset being paid; selects native vs ERC20 in the\n    ///                     fee leg.\n    /// @param  gross       Pre-fee borrower payout amount.\n    /// @return toUser      `gross` minus a transferred fee, or full `gross` on\n    ///                     any non-charging path.\n    function chargeExitFeeAndPay(\n        bytes32 surfaceId,\n        address subProduct,\n        address receiver,\n        address payoutAsset,\n        uint256 gross\n    ) public payable returns (uint256 toUser) {\n        if (gross == 0) return 0;\n\n        IExitFeeController.ExitFeeQuote memory q = PerimeterLib.safeQuote(\n            PerimeterLib.getController(),\n            surfaceId,\n            subProduct,\n            msg.sender,\n            gross\n        );\n\n        if (q.active && q.feeAmount > 0) {\n            if (!PerimeterLib.quoteIsValid(q, gross)) {\n                emit ExitFeeSkipped(\n                    surfaceId,\n                    msg.sender,\n                    payoutAsset,\n                    gross,\n                    q.rateBps,\n                    uint8(IExitFeeController.SkipReason.INVALID_QUOTE)\n                );\n                return gross;\n            }\n            bool feeOk = _payExitFeeLeg(q.feeReceiver, payoutAsset, q.feeAmount);\n            if (feeOk) {\n                emit ExitFeeApplied(\n                    surfaceId,\n                    msg.sender,\n                    payoutAsset,\n                    subProduct,\n                    receiver,\n                    gross,\n                    q.feeAmount,\n                    q.netAmount,\n                    q.feeReceiver\n                );\n                return q.netAmount;\n            }\n            emit ExitFeeSkipped(\n                surfaceId,\n                msg.sender,\n                payoutAsset,\n                gross,\n                q.rateBps,\n                uint8(IExitFeeController.SkipReason.VAULT_REVERT)\n            );\n            return gross;\n        }\n        emit ExitFeeSkipped(surfaceId, msg.sender, payoutAsset, gross, q.rateBps, q.reason);\n        return gross;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Escrow the (post-fee) borrower-exit user leg into the queue.\n    ///         PUSH-then-record via the `sovrynProtocol` singleton (the registered\n    ///         allowed source): the vault primitive sends `toUser` to the queue and\n    ///         the queue credits it via measured-delta.\n    ///\n    ///         Called ONLY once the caller has resolved a delay (`d > 0`), so the\n    ///         queue is never touched on a direct-pay exit. Runs under\n    ///         `delegatecall` in the protocol proxy's context, so the vault\n    ///         primitives spend protocol balances. FAIL-CLOSED throughout: an\n    ///         unresolvable queue or a rejected record reverts, and the caller\n    ///         propagates that so the whole exit reverts.\n    /// @param  subProduct  Policy resolution key \u2014 the iToken proxy the loan was\n    ///                     originated against (`loanLocal.lender`).\n    /// @param  assetToken  Withdraw token (address == wrbtcToken \u21d2 native leg).\n    /// @param  receiver    Immutable payout destination.\n    /// @param  toUser      Net (post-fee) borrower payout amount.\n    /// @param  d           Delay in seconds, already resolved by the caller.\n    /// @param  effOrig     The originator recorded for the request.\n    /// @param  effOwner    The owner recorded for the request.\n    /// @return escrowed    Always true; a failure reverts instead.\n    function escrowBorrowerExit(\n        address subProduct,\n        address assetToken,\n        address receiver,\n        uint256 toUser,\n        uint32 d,\n        address effOrig,\n        address effOwner\n    ) public payable returns (bool escrowed) {\n        DelayLeg memory leg;\n        leg.receiver = receiver;\n        leg.toUser = toUser;\n        leg.subProduct = subProduct;\n        leg.d = d;\n        leg.effOrig = effOrig;\n        leg.effOwner = effOwner;\n\n        leg.queue = PerimeterLib.getExitDelayQueue();\n        require(leg.queue != address(0), \"PERIMETER:queue-unset\");\n\n        // PUSH to the queue, then measured-record \u2014 both in the SAME outer tx, so\n        // a record revert rolls back the push (fail-closed).\n        if (assetToken == address(wrbtcToken)) {\n            // native leg: unwrap WRBTC \u2192 native RBTC into the queue's receive().\n            leg.token = address(0);\n            vaultEtherWithdraw(leg.queue, toUser);\n        } else {\n            leg.token = assetToken;\n            vaultWithdraw(assetToken, leg.queue, toUser);\n        }\n        _recordBorrowerExitToQueue(leg);\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Record a borrower-exit user leg into the queue AFTER the caller has\n    ///         PUSHED `toUser` to it (measured-delta ingress). The queue measures\n    ///         the non-backing surplus, requires it `>= toUser`, and credits\n    ///         EXACTLY `toUser` \u2014 so a stray donation can never brick the record.\n    function _recordBorrowerExitToQueue(DelayLeg memory leg) internal {\n        require(leg.toUser <= uint256(uint128(-1)), \"PERIMETER:amount-too-large\");\n        if (leg.token == address(0)) {\n            IExitDelayQueueHook(leg.queue).recordReceivedNativeExit(\n                uint128(leg.toUser),\n                leg.d,\n                PERIMETER_SURFACE_LENDING_BORROWER_WITHDRAW,\n                leg.subProduct,\n                leg.effOrig,\n                leg.effOwner,\n                leg.receiver\n            );\n        } else {\n            IExitDelayQueueHook(leg.queue).recordReceivedERC20Exit(\n                leg.token,\n                uint128(leg.toUser),\n                leg.d,\n                PERIMETER_SURFACE_LENDING_BORROWER_WITHDRAW,\n                leg.subProduct,\n                leg.effOrig,\n                leg.effOwner,\n                leg.receiver\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Fail-open fee-leg transfer: returns false on any transfer\n    ///         failure instead of reverting, so the caller can fall back to a\n    ///         full-gross payout.\n    ///         - Native (asset == wrbtcToken): unwrap, low-level `call.value`;\n    ///           on failure re-wrap so no native residue remains.\n    ///         - ERC20: low-level `transfer` with a length-gated bool decode.\n    function _payExitFeeLeg(\n        address receiver,\n        address asset,\n        uint256 amount\n    ) internal returns (bool) {\n        if (amount == 0) return true;\n        if (asset == address(wrbtcToken)) {\n            uint256 balance = address(this).balance;\n            if (amount > balance) {\n                wrbtcToken.withdraw(amount - balance);\n            }\n            (bool ok, ) = receiver.call.value(amount)(\"\");\n            if (ok) return true;\n            // Re-wrap on failure: native back into WRBTC, no orphan native,\n            // no WRBTC underflow against the protocol's vault accounting.\n            wrbtcToken.deposit.value(amount)();\n            return false;\n        }\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = asset.call(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC20(asset).transfer.selector, receiver, amount)\n        );\n        if (!ok) return false;\n        if (ret.length == 0) return true;\n        if (ret.length != 32) return false;\n        return abi.decode(ret, (bool));\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0x5305c1910a3614a82b89abade7cd08ada94b083467c094695d5a62f85946c9a5"},"contracts/utils/PerimeterLib.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.5.17;\npragma experimental ABIEncoderV2;\n\nimport \"../interfaces/perimeter/IExitFeeController.sol\";\n\n/// @title  PerimeterLib\n/// @notice Storage-free Perimeter plumbing: the controller/ops slot accessors and\n///         the quote helpers. `internal` functions are inlined into the caller,\n///         so the slot accessors operate on the caller's storage and the\n///         library is never deployed.\nlibrary PerimeterLib {\n    // \u2500\u2500\u2500 Controller pointer \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\n    /// @notice EIP-1967-style unstructured slot where each consumer pins its\n    ///         ExitFeeController. Defined once here so the getter and setter\n    ///         can never drift onto different slots.\n    /// keccak256(\"sovryn.perimeterExitFeeController\") - 1\n    bytes32 internal constant EXIT_FEE_CONTROLLER_SLOT =\n        bytes32(uint256(keccak256(\"sovryn.perimeterExitFeeController\")) - 1);\n\n    /// @notice Read the calling contract's pinned controller from the shared\n    ///         slot (address(0) until the owner pins one). Inlined, so the\n    ///         `sload` targets the caller's storage.\n    function getController() internal view returns (address ctrl) {\n        bytes32 slot = EXIT_FEE_CONTROLLER_SLOT;\n        assembly {\n            ctrl := sload(slot)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Write the calling contract's controller pointer. The caller\n    ///         owns authorization, the `Address.isContract` guard, and the\n    ///         `ExitFeeControllerSet` event; this performs only the slot write\n    ///         (inlined into the caller's storage).\n    function setController(address ctrl) internal {\n        bytes32 slot = EXIT_FEE_CONTROLLER_SLOT;\n        assembly {\n            sstore(slot, ctrl)\n        }\n    }\n\n    // \u2500\u2500\u2500 Borrower-exit Ops pointer \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\n    /// @notice EIP-1967-style unstructured slot holding the borrower-exit\n    ///         charge-hook (`BorrowerExitPerimeterOps`) address.\n    /// @dev The literal is the slot address: this pointer lives at an\n    ///      unstructured slot derived from the string, not at a position fixed\n    ///      by declaration order. Changing the string moves the slot, so the\n    ///      pointer must be re-pinned at the new address before the hook is\n    ///      reachable.\n    /// keccak256(\"sovryn.perimeterBorrowerExitOps\") - 1\n    bytes32 internal constant BORROWER_EXIT_PERIMETER_OPS_SLOT =\n        bytes32(uint256(keccak256(\"sovryn.perimeterBorrowerExitOps\")) - 1);\n\n    /// @notice Read the pinned charge-hook address (address(0) until pinned).\n    ///         Inlined `sload` against the caller's storage.\n    function getBorrowerExitOps() internal view returns (address ops) {\n        bytes32 slot = BORROWER_EXIT_PERIMETER_OPS_SLOT;\n        assembly {\n            ops := sload(slot)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Write the charge-hook pointer (caller owns auth + the event).\n    function setBorrowerExitOps(address ops) internal {\n        bytes32 slot = BORROWER_EXIT_PERIMETER_OPS_SLOT;\n        assembly {\n            sstore(slot, ops)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Fail-open read of `host`'s pinned controller via its public\n    ///         `exitFeeController()` view. Any abnormal outcome \u2014 no code at\n    ///         `host`, unregistered selector, short/long return \u2014 yields\n    ///         address(0), which `safeQuote` treats as \"skip\", so the lookup\n    ///         can never block an exit.\n    ///\n    /// @dev    POINTER lookup is FAIL-OPEN, QUOTE is FAIL-CLOSED.\n    ///         This is a deliberate, documented split:\n    ///           \u2022 A missing/unreachable controller POINTER (address(0) here)\n    ///             skips BOTH the fee and the delay reroute and pays direct \u2014\n    ///             mirroring the fee path. A fail-CLOSED read-through would\n    ///             brick EVERY lender exit on a botched module rotation, so the\n    ///             pointer read must never revert.\n    ///           \u2022 Once a controller IS reachable, the delay QUOTE\n    ///             (`safeQuoteDelay` \u2192 `quoteExitDelayFor`) stays FAIL-CLOSED\n    ///             a quote that reverts reverts the whole exit, so\n    ///             an active perimeter can never be silently bypassed.\n    ///         Accepted residual: a missing pointer silently disables the\n    ///         perimeter for that host until the Owner re-pins it. This is NOT\n    ///         attacker-reachable (setting the pointer is an Owner/SIP action).\n    ///         The go-live wiring assertion reads every live host's controller\n    ///         pointer back and requires it to equal the deployed controller \u2014\n    ///         the same per-host loop that already requires the queue pointer to\n    ///         match \u2014 so a host going live with no controller pinned, or one\n    ///         knocked back to zero before go-live, is refused. That gate runs\n    ///         once, before activation; a pointer knocked back to zero AFTER\n    ///         go-live is caught only by off-chain pointer monitoring, not by\n    ///         this assertion.\n    function safeControllerLookup(address host) internal view returns (address) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = host.staticcall(\n            abi.encodeWithSignature(\"exitFeeController()\")\n        );\n        if (ok && ret.length == 32) {\n            return abi.decode(ret, (address));\n        }\n        return address(0);\n    }\n\n    // \u2500\u2500\u2500 Exit-delay queue pointer (security perimeter) \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\n    /// @notice EIP-1967-style unstructured slot where each product storage host\n    ///         pins its ExitDelayQueue. Because the queue pointer redirects\n    ///         ESCROW it is MORE sensitive than the controller pointer \u2014 rotation\n    ///         is an Owner/SIP action. Defined once so the\n    ///         getter and setter can never drift onto different slots.\n    /// keccak256(\"sovryn.perimeterExitDelayQueue\") - 1\n    bytes32 internal constant EXIT_DELAY_QUEUE_SLOT =\n        bytes32(uint256(keccak256(\"sovryn.perimeterExitDelayQueue\")) - 1);\n\n    /// @notice Read the calling contract's pinned queue from the shared slot\n    ///         (address(0) until the Owner pins one). An unwired queue pays\n    ///         direct ONLY when the perimeter quotes `d == 0`; once `d > 0` the\n    ///         caller must escrow, so an unresolvable queue fails CLOSED (the\n    ///         exit reverts) \u2014 a delay can never be silently bypassed by an\n    ///         unwired pointer. Inlined, so the `sload` targets the caller's\n    ///         storage.\n    function getExitDelayQueue() internal view returns (address queue) {\n        bytes32 slot = EXIT_DELAY_QUEUE_SLOT;\n        assembly {\n            queue := sload(slot)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Write the calling contract's queue pointer (caller owns auth, the\n    ///         `Address.isContract` guard, and the event). Inlined into the\n    ///         caller's storage.\n    function setExitDelayQueue(address queue) internal {\n        bytes32 slot = EXIT_DELAY_QUEUE_SLOT;\n        assembly {\n            sstore(slot, queue)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Fail-open read of `host`'s pinned queue via its public\n    ///         `exitDelayQueue()` view. Any abnormal outcome (no code at `host`,\n    ///         unregistered selector, short/long return) yields address(0). The\n    ///         lookup itself is view-only and never touches the queue, so it\n    ///         cannot brick anything; but note that a resulting address(0) pays\n    ///         direct ONLY when the perimeter quotes `d == 0`. When `d > 0` the\n    ///         caller escrows, so an unresolvable queue then fails CLOSED at the\n    ///         escrow step (the exit reverts until the queue is wired) \u2014 an\n    ///         unwired queue cannot silently bypass an active delay.\n    function safeQueueLookup(address host) internal view returns (address) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = host.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(\"exitDelayQueue()\"));\n        if (ok && ret.length == 32) {\n            return abi.decode(ret, (address));\n        }\n        return address(0);\n    }\n\n    // \u2500\u2500\u2500 Delay quote (per-pragma safe-quote wrapper) \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\n    /// @notice Fail-CLOSED delay quote: `quoteExitDelayFor` via `staticcall`\n    ///         (0.5.17 has no try/catch). A staticcall FAILURE reverts the exit \u2014\n    ///         it MUST NOT be interpreted as `d = 0`-direct (that would silently\n    ///         disable the perimeter \u2014 the hazard this guards against). The\n    ///         `!securityPerimeterEnabled` short-circuit is the FIRST statement\n    ///         inside `quoteExitDelayFor`, so a\n    ///         healthy-but-disabled perimeter returns `(0, raw, owner)` normally\n    ///         (liveness); only a fully-bricked controller (bad upgrade) is\n    ///         unescapable, and the go-live gates cover it.\n    ///\n    ///         The return is decoded word-wise (three static words) and each is\n    ///         bounds-checked, mirroring `safeQuote`'s defensive decode so a\n    ///         malformed controller return reverts loudly (fail-closed) rather than\n    ///         mis-escrowing.\n    /// @param  ctrl The caller's pinned ExitFeeController (address(0) \u21d2 perimeter\n    ///              unwired \u21d2 direct pay, d = 0).\n    function safeQuoteDelay(\n        address ctrl,\n        address rawOriginator,\n        address owner,\n        address receiver,\n        bytes32 surfaceId,\n        address subProduct\n    ) internal view returns (uint32 d, address effOrig, address effOwner) {\n        // No controller pinned \u21d2 perimeter is unwired; pay direct (d = 0). Raw\n        // identities are returned but the hook ignores them when d == 0.\n        if (ctrl == address(0)) {\n            return (0, rawOriginator, owner);\n        }\n        (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = ctrl.staticcall(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(\n                IExitFeeController(ctrl).quoteExitDelayFor.selector,\n                rawOriginator,\n                owner,\n                receiver,\n                surfaceId,\n                subProduct\n            )\n        );\n        // FAIL-CLOSED: a staticcall failure or a short/malformed return reverts\n        // the exit. 3 static words = 96 bytes (uint32 d, address effOrig,\n        // address effOwner). Decode as RAW WORDS then bounds-check each \u2014 a\n        // uint256-tuple decode cannot revert on any >= 96-byte payload, so we\n        // control the revert reason instead of letting the validating decoder\n        // brick the exit with an opaque panic.\n        require(ok && ret.length >= 96, \"PERIMETER:delay-quote-failed\");\n        (uint256 rawD, uint256 rawOrig, uint256 rawOwner) = abi.decode(\n            ret,\n            (uint256, uint256, uint256)\n        );\n        require(\n            rawD <= 0xffffffff && rawOrig >> 160 == 0 && rawOwner >> 160 == 0,\n            \"PERIMETER:delay-quote-malformed\"\n        );\n        d = uint32(rawD);\n        effOrig = address(uint160(rawOrig));\n        effOwner = address(uint160(rawOwner));\n    }\n\n    // \u2500\u2500\u2500 Quote \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n\n    /// @notice Quote the fee for an exit, failing open on any non-ideal\n    ///         outcome (controller not pinned, controller revert, short\n    ///         return). Solidity 0.5.17 has no `try/catch`, so the only way\n    ///         to keep the burn/exit alive when the controller misbehaves is\n    ///         to go through `staticcall` rather than a direct interface call.\n    ///         Semantic validation of the returned quote lives in\n    ///         `quoteIsValid`, not here.\n    /// @param ctrl The caller's pinned ExitFeeController (address(0) => skip).\n    function safeQuote(\n        address ctrl,\n        bytes32 surfaceId,\n        address subProduct,\n        address actor,\n        uint256 gross\n    ) internal view returns (IExitFeeController.ExitFeeQuote memory q) {\n        if (ctrl != address(0)) {\n            (bool ok, bytes memory ret) = ctrl.staticcall(\n                abi.encodeWithSelector(\n                    IExitFeeController(ctrl).quoteExitFee.selector,\n                    surfaceId,\n                    subProduct,\n                    actor,\n                    gross\n                )\n            );\n            // 6 static fields \u00d7 32 bytes = 192-byte canonical encoding of\n            // `(ExitFeeQuote)`. Decode as RAW WORDS first \u2014 a uint256-tuple\n            // decode cannot revert on any >= 192-byte payload \u2014 then bounds-\n            // check each word for its target type. Decoding the struct\n            // directly would let the 0.5.17 validating decoder revert on a\n            // non-canonical word (bool > 1, dirty uint16/address upper bits),\n            // and on the inline iToken path that revert would brick the burn\n            // instead of failing open. Malformed words route to\n            // CONTROLLER_REVERT below; extra trailing bytes are tolerated; a\n            // short return is rejected by the length gate.\n            if (ok && ret.length >= 192) {\n                (\n                    uint256 rawActive,\n                    uint256 rawRateBps,\n                    uint256 feeAmount,\n                    uint256 netAmount,\n                    uint256 rawReceiver,\n                    uint256 rawReason\n                ) = abi.decode(ret, (uint256, uint256, uint256, uint256, uint256, uint256));\n                if (\n                    rawActive <= 1 &&\n                    rawRateBps <= 0xffff &&\n                    rawReceiver >> 160 == 0 &&\n                    rawReason <= 0xff\n                ) {\n                    q.active = rawActive == 1;\n                    q.rateBps = uint16(rawRateBps);\n                    q.feeAmount = feeAmount;\n                    q.netAmount = netAmount;\n                    q.feeReceiver = address(uint160(rawReceiver));\n                    q.reason = uint8(rawReason);\n                    return q;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // Fail open: pretend the controller returned an inactive quote.\n        q.netAmount = gross;\n        q.reason = uint8(IExitFeeController.SkipReason.CONTROLLER_REVERT);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Defensive sanity-check on a quote returned by the (upgradable,\n    ///      external) controller. A misconfigured or hostile controller could\n    ///      overpay from pool liquidity, send fee value to address(0), or\n    ///      desync net+fee from gross. Failure routes to INVALID_QUOTE.\n    function quoteIsValid(\n        IExitFeeController.ExitFeeQuote memory q,\n        uint256 gross\n    ) internal pure returns (bool) {\n        if (q.feeReceiver == address(0)) return false;\n        if (q.feeAmount > gross) return false;\n        // `gross - q.feeAmount` cannot underflow because of the check above.\n        // Phrasing the invariant as \"net == gross - fee\" instead of\n        // \"fee + net == gross\" avoids the unchecked addition that 0.5.17\n        // would otherwise allow to wrap.\n        if (q.netAmount != gross - q.feeAmount) return false;\n        if (q.rateBps > 10_000) return false;\n        return true;\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0xd2238dfd2f61c1dc44d19cc28783042d30dd697054be730cf4a725c601f77d7a"}},"version":1}

devdoc.details: Runs only under `delegatecall` in the calling proxy's context:         storage is the proxy's (controller pointer, `wrbtcToken`),         `address(this)` is the proxy (the fee leg spends protocol         balances), and `msg.sender` is the exiting actor. Declares no         storage of its own.  ///         Fail-open: a misbehaving controller, an invalid quote, or a failed         fee transfer each resolve to "charge nothing, pay full gross". A         direct (non-delegatecall) call runs against this contract's own         empty storage and it holds no funds, so it is an inert no-op.

chargeExitFeeAndPay(bytes32,address,addr.notice: Split a borrower-side exit payout into fee + net: quote,         validate, pay the fee leg, emit the audit event, and return the         amount the caller pays the user (the caller does the user-leg         payout on its own vault primitives).

escrowBorrowerExit(address,address,addre.notice: Escrow the (post-fee) borrower-exit user leg into the queue.         PUSH-then-record via the `sovrynProtocol` singleton (the registered         allowed source): the vault primitive sends `toUser` to the queue and         the queue credits it via measured-delta.     ///         Called ONLY once the caller has resolved a delay (`d > 0`), so the         queue is never touched on a direct-pay exit. Runs under         `delegatecall` in the protocol proxy's context, so the vault         primitives spend protocol balances. FAIL-CLOSED throughout: an         unresolvable queue or a rejected record reverts, and the caller         propagates that so the whole exit reverts.
